clue.text: Intimate that I'd go in and put the frighteners on!

indicators.note: go in tells us the letters of I'd are placed inside the word intimate

parts.note: taken as written: intimate as a verb, to hint
I'd without its apostrophe gives the two letters

explanation.surface: Hinting that someone will turn up and scare them, a gangster's veiled threat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intimate' looks like an adjective (close), but here it is the verb meaning to hint, taken whole as the container.
explanation.definitionFit: To put the frighteners on someone is a British idiom for scaring or threatening them into compliance.

clue.text: Italian child's irritating sensation

parts.note: IT is a standard abbreviation for Italian (as in Italian vermouth, 'gin and it')

explanation.surface: An Italian youngster suffering some annoying skin complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: An urge to scratch is the classic annoying feeling on the skin.

clue.text: It's pointedly found at the end of a fork

definitions.text: It's pointedly found at the end of a fork

parts.words: It's pointedly found at the end of a fork
parts.note: pointedly reads both as 'emphatically' and literally as 'with a sharp point': the prongs of a fork are what sit at its end

explanation.surface: Someone stresses that a thing turns up at the end of a fork in the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fork' suggests a branching road, but it is the cutlery, whose sharp prongs are at its end.
explanation.definitionFit: A prong of a fork or of a deer's antler is called by this word.

clue.text: Fungus on beer you and I brought up

parts.note: mild is a dark, lightly hopped British beer

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means the letters for you and I are read from bottom to top

parts.note: you and I together are we

explanation.surface: Mould growing on the beer that the two of us hauled up from the cellar.
explanation.walkthrough: MILD is a British style of beer; 'brought up' turns WE into EW beneath it in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a whitish growth caused by fungi on plants and damp surfaces.

clue.text: Suitable place for the lift to go?

definitions.text: place for the lift to go?

explanation.surface: Asking where an elevator would sensibly end up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suits me down to the ground' is the idiom for perfectly suitable; read literally, the ground floor is where a lift heads when going down.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means completely or perfectly fitting, and the literal reading is the lowest floor, where a descending elevator ends.

clue.text: Stitched using sound diplomacy

indicators.note: sound here is the signal that the word for diplomacy is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: tact is skill and sensitivity in dealing with others

explanation.surface: Something sewn together by means of wise diplomatic handling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound diplomacy' reads as wise statecraft, but 'sound' signals that TACT said aloud gives the word.
explanation.definitionFit: To tack is to sew loosely with long temporary stitches.

clue.text: Revise decree that's not clear initially

indicators.note: not tells us the letter that follows is to be dropped from the word for decree

parts.note: an edict is an official decree or proclamation

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letter of the word clear

explanation.surface: Amend an official ruling whose wording is not clear at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes C from 'clear'; 'not' removes it from EDICT.
explanation.definitionFit: To revise text is to correct and amend it, the job of an editor.

clue.text: Dishearten although it's belonging to us in record time

indicators.note: in puts the word for belonging to us inside the joined words for record and time

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
an age is a long period of time
ours is what belongs to us, giving our

explanation.surface: Feeling low even though our group has a new record time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'although it's' is padding for the surface; 'record' is a gramophone disc, not a best performance.
explanation.definitionFit: To dishearten someone is to sap their confidence and resolve, deterring them.

clue.text: The unluckiest one to follow dozen others

explanation.surface: The most ill-fated person, following a dozen others in line.
explanation.walkthrough: Thirteen is the traditionally unlucky number; the item numbered thirteen comes straight after a dozen.
explanation.definitionFit: The ordinal for thirteen names the one coming after twelve, and thirteen is the superstitious unlucky number.

clue.text: Inflammable material?

parts.note: material read as fabric points to a tufted cotton cloth, while inflammable points to the burning string in a candle

explanation.surface: A question about stuff that catches fire easily.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is both a tufted cotton fabric used for bedspreads and literally the wick of a candle, which is meant to burn.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a soft tufted cotton fabric, and literally it is the cord that burns in a candle.

clue.text: Some fascinating enlarged cells

indicators.note: some signals that only part of the word fascinating is taken, from inside it

explanation.surface: Some intriguing cells that have been magnified.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes the letters from inside fASCInating.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the sac-shaped spore-bearing cells of certain fungi, larger than surrounding cells; the word is a plural.

clue.text: Supporting part share

parts.note: pro means in favour of or supporting
a portion is a part or piece of something

explanation.surface: A partial stake that props something up.
explanation.definitionFit: A proportion is a fraction or allotted part of a whole.

clue.text: In all directions at each place in question

parts.note: every means each one of a group
where is the word that asks which place

explanation.surface: Spreading out every way from each point being discussed.
explanation.definitionFit: Throughout every place, all around, spread on all sides.

clue.text: The girl who found it was hot inside kettle

indicators.note: inside places the letter for hot within the word for kettle

parts.note: a kettle is a device for heating water, so a heater
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A girl discovers it has become hot inside the kettle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The girl' is a definition by example: any girl's name fits the definition, so the wordplay must pin down which.
explanation.definitionFit: A common female first name, so an example of a girl.

clue.text: That woman on the railway found the birds' breeding-place

parts.note: her refers to a woman already mentioned
taken as written
RY is a standard abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A woman on a train spots where birds nest.
explanation.definitionFit: A colony where herons nest and rear young is so called.

clue.text: Come back with fresh cover?

explanation.surface: A comeback for something newly wrapped.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word as re-bound, a book bound again in a new cover.
explanation.definitionFit: To spring back after hitting something; also a book given new binding.

clue.text: Survey about the picture of the scene

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in letters
a view is a sight or picture of a landscape

explanation.surface: Inspecting a painting of a landscape.
explanation.definitionFit: To survey something is to examine or assess it as a whole.

clue.text: From in Paris, five excluded were pious

parts.note: de is French for from
V is the Roman numeral five
out means left out or excluded

explanation.surface: Five Parisians were left out because they were too religious.
explanation.definitionFit: Deeply religious and devoted in worship.

clue.text: What usually happens at the links

definitions.text: What usually happens at the links

parts.words: What usually happens at the links
parts.note: links is a golf course, where the standard score for the round is literally that, and the idiom means what is normal

explanation.surface: A description of the typical events on a golf course.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom means what is to be expected; literally, par is the standard score for a golf course, and links is a seaside golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means normal or expected, from golf's standard score for a round.

clue.text: Retired draughtsman received recompense

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn or gone back, so the word for draughtsman is read backwards

parts.note: a drawer is one who draws, a draughtsman

explanation.surface: A drafting draughtsman who has retired was paid off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' turns DRAWER around to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Payment or prize given in return for a service.

clue.text: Be upstanding in time for discussion

indicators.note: in places the turned letters inside the word for time

parts.note: a date is a particular point in time

indicators.note: upstanding in a down entry means the word be is written bottom to top

explanation.surface: An invitation for everyone to rise in time for the talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Be upstanding' is the formal call for a room to rise; here 'upstanding' turns the letters bottom to top in this down entry, giving EB.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal argument in which opposing views are put forward.

clue.text: Man on board during the hours of darkness was heard

indicators.note: was heard signals that the word for the hours of darkness is spoken, giving a word said the same way

parts.note: night is the period of darkness

explanation.surface: A man on a ship at night made a noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man on board' looks like a sailor, but it is a chess piece on the board.
explanation.definitionFit: A chess piece is called a man, and this one moves in an L shape.

clue.text: Wailer is more penetrating

explanation.surface: A mourner who cries is sharper.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is a mourner who keens, an Irish lament for the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: One who keens laments loudly over the dead; also comparative of an adjective meaning sharp.

clue.text: For several months Edward had a craving

parts.note: a year is twelve months
Ned is a familiar form of Edward

explanation.surface: Edward longed for something for months.
explanation.definitionFit: Longed for something deeply.

clue.text: I left old holly

parts.note: ex means former or old

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned an old holly bush.
explanation.definitionFit: The botanical genus name for the holly is used as its common name too.

clue.text: Shade right of centre

explanation.surface: A tint that leans to the political right.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain this colour stands for the Conservative Party, so politically right of centre.
explanation.definitionFit: A colour of the sky; also British slang for Conservative, the party of the moderate right.

clue.text: Perch on a rock in the north sea

definitions.text: a rock in the north sea

explanation.surface: Something sitting on a rock in the north sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perch' looks like a verb but it is a fish; the second sense is the Bass Rock, an island in the Firth of Forth, Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A perch-like sea fish; also the Bass Rock, a famous Scottish island off the east coast.

clue.text: Unrestrained Australian revelry

indicators.note: unrestrained means let loose, so the letters of Australian are rearranged

explanation.surface: Wild Aussie partying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unrestrained' looks like it describes the revelry, but it rearranges AUSTRALIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman winter festival, now any riotous merrymaking.

clue.text: Votes against feature soundly

indicators.note: soundly signals the word for feature is to be said aloud

parts.note: a nose is a facial feature

explanation.surface: Votes against are strongly characteristic.
explanation.definitionFit: Negative votes, as cried in a division of Parliament.

clue.text: Both poles resented unusual compassion

indicators.note: unusual means abnormal, so the combined letters are rearranged

parts.note: N is north pole
S is south pole

explanation.surface: Explorers at north and south both resent unusual kindness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' shuffles N and RESENTED into TENDERNES; the second pole, S, ends the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Gentle kindness and affection.
